definitions.explanation: A body of water partially enclosed by land, forming an indentation in the coastline. Used in geographical and maritime contexts.

examples.japanese: {海湾|かいわん}に{船|ふね}が{停泊|ていはく}している。
examples.english: Ships are anchored in the bay.

examples.japanese: この{海湾|かいわん}は{天然|てんねん}の{良港|りょうこう}として{知|し}られている。
examples.english: This bay is known as a natural good harbor.

examples.japanese: {海湾|かいわん}{沿|ぞ}いの{地域|ちいき}では、{漁業|ぎょぎょう}と{観光|かんこう}が{主|おも}な{産業|さんぎょう}になっている。
examples.english: In the areas along the bay, fishing and tourism are the main industries.

notes:
A compound of {海|かい} (sea) and {湾|わん} (bay), used as a slightly more formal or literary term for a bay or gulf. In everyday speech, {湾|わん} alone is more common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {海湾|かいわん}{地域|ちいき}: bay area; gulf region
- {海湾|かいわん}{沿|ぞ}い: along the bay
- {海湾|かいわん}{諸国|しょこく}: gulf states (as in the Persian Gulf countries)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {湾|わん}: bay; gulf (the standard, more common term)
- {入|い}り{江|え}: inlet; cove (smaller than a bay)
- {内海|ないかい}: inland sea (a sea largely enclosed by land)

USAGE:
The term {海湾|かいわん} appears in formal or geographical contexts. In news coverage of the Middle East, {海湾|かいわん}{戦争|せんそう} (Gulf War) and {海湾|かいわん}{諸国|しょこく} (Gulf states) are commonly encountered usages.
